Salah
sā'lä
n. (the son of Arphaxad and father of Eber in the line from Shem to Abraham; written Shelah in the Chronicles and Sala by Luke)
From Hebrew Shelach, generally rendered a sending forth or a sprout, a shoot, from shalach, to send. The Authorized Version writes him Salah in Genesis and Shelah in 1 Chronicles 1:18; Luke gives the Greek Sala. He is a different man altogether from Shelah the third son of Judah, who has his own entry in this dictionary.

Biblical Definition

Salah stands third in the postdiluvian line, between Arphaxad and Eber: “And Arphaxad begat Salah; and Salah begat Eber” (Gen 10:24), with the dates supplied in the register of Genesis 11: “And Arphaxad lived five and thirty years, and begat Salah” (Gen 11:12), and “And Salah lived thirty years, and begat Eber” (Gen 11:14), living four hundred and three years afterward. The Chronicler spells him Shelah in the compressed roll: “Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah” (1Ch 1:24). His importance lies wholly in the son. Eber is the man from whom the name Hebrew is generally traced, and Genesis marks him out specially: Shem is called “the father of all the children of Eber” (Gen 10:21), and it was in the days of Eber's son Peleg that the earth was divided. So Salah sits at the narrowing of the line: from all mankind after the flood, to Shem, to Arphaxad, to Salah, to Eber, and on down through Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor and Terah to Abram — the funnel by which the promise made to the woman's seed is brought to one household in Mesopotamia. Luke walks the same names backward: “which was the son of Heber, which was the son of Sala” (Luk 3:35).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Salah; in sacred history he is the son of Arphaxad and the father of Eber, in the line from Shem to Abraham.

expand to see more

SALAH, n. A sending forth, a shoot; the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem.

He is written Shelah in the first book of Chronicles, and Sala by Luke.

He lived thirty years and begat Eber, and four hundred and three years after.

From Eber his son the name of the Hebrews is commonly derived.

He is not the same with Shelah the son of Judah, who was born at Chezib.

Gen 10:24 — "And Arphaxad begat Salah; and Salah begat Eber."

Modern Corruption

There is no significant modern redefinition of this name. The principle to recover is that God narrows the line of promise deliberately, name by name, and that election is visible in Scripture as a family tree long before it is stated as a doctrine.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Salah is a name in the register and nobody has contested him. What the postdiluvian genealogy sets before the reader is a narrowing. Genesis 10 spreads out into seventy nations, the whole earth peopled from three sons; Genesis 11 then takes one of those sons and follows a single thread through nine generations to one man in Ur. The Bible is the story of that thread. It does not lose interest in the nations — the promise to Abram is that in him all families of the earth shall be blessed — but the route to the many runs through the one.

The principle to recover is that election is not an abstraction bolted onto the gospel by later theologians; it is the shape of the narrative from Genesis 4 onward. Abel not Cain, Seth not the line of Lamech, Shem not Ham, Isaac not Ishmael, Jacob not Esau, Judah not Reuben. Paul draws the conclusion from exactly this material: “So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy” (Rom 9:16). A reader who finds the doctrine strange has not yet noticed how the genealogies are built.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Shelach (H7974), Salah, Shelah; shalach (H7971), to send, send forth; 'Eber (H5677), Eber; 'Arpakshad (H775), Arphaxad; Greek Sala (G4527).

expand to see more

Hebrew Shelach (H7974) — Salah; son of Arphaxad, father of Eber.

Hebrew shalach (H7971) — to send forth; the root of the name.

Hebrew 'Eber (H5677) — Eber; his son, from whom the Hebrews are named.

Hebrew 'Arpakshad (H775) — Arphaxad; his father, born two years after the flood.

Greek Sala (G4527) — the form Luke uses in the genealogy of Christ.

Usage

"“And Arphaxad begat Salah; and Salah begat Eber” — two links of the narrowing line."

"“Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah” — the Chronicler's compressed spelling."

"“Which was the son of Sala” — Luke tracing the Lord's descent through him."
